claims.claim_text: The old definition stopped working: proof production and verification are being automated, while choosing what to prove stayed human.
claims.evidence_quote: The production of proofs has been automated, or it will be, under Tao's working assumption. (¶10) ... that is being automated too. (¶14)
claims.reasoning: Source states both production and verification are automated or will be, and problem choosing stays human.

claims.claim_text: A professor's post: research now feels like grading a clever student desperate for an A who does not mind lying.
claims.evidence_quote: his research has started to feel like grading the proofs of a very clever student who is desperate to get an A and doesn't mind lying to do so (¶1)
claims.reasoning: Matches the quoted professor's post verbatim in meaning.

claims.claim_text: The old definition: mathematics is the discipline of finding patterns where claims can be proven.
claims.evidence_quote: Mathematics is the discipline of finding patterns where claims can be proven. (¶3)
claims.reasoning: Direct quote of the author's old definition.

claims.claim_text: Under that definition mathematics was the production of correct statements, though mathematicians built intuition and found clues to patterns.
claims.evidence_quote: Under the old definition, mathematics was the production of correct statements ... they're building intuitioin and finding clues to find patterns (¶10)
claims.reasoning: Source makes both points, the production framing and the intuition/clue-finding caveat.

claims.claim_text: Experts could settle whether an idea was right, most of the time, which set math apart from fields with opinions, even physics.
claims.evidence_quote: a community of experts can settle which, for good, well, most of the times ... different from art criticism, politics, business, psychology, biology, or even physics (¶4)
claims.reasoning: Preserves the 'most of the times' hedge and the physics contrast.

claims.claim_text: In summer 2026 Tao's ICM lecture and Moradifam's essay asked what mathematics is once proof production stops being scarce.
claims.evidence_quote: The summer of 2026 ... Terence Tao gave a public lecture ... Amir Moradifam published an essay ... when the production of proofs stops being scarce (¶5)
claims.reasoning: Names, venue, date, and framing all match the source.

claims.claim_text: The author mostly agrees, but they stop where he must speculate; he wants to push past that edge.
claims.evidence_quote: I ... mostly agree with them. However, they stop at the edge of the question I want to push on: the next step is speculation (¶5)
claims.reasoning: Matches the author's stated agreement and desire to push past the edge.

claims.claim_text: First Proof's late May 2026 test: four leading systems solved seven of ten unpublished research problems to publication quality.
claims.evidence_quote: ran a standardized test ... in late May 2026: four leading systems solved seven of ten unpublished problems to publication quality (¶8)
claims.reasoning: All numbers (four, seven, ten) and date match source.

claims.claim_text: Compute cost ten to a thousand dollars per problem.
claims.evidence_quote: for ten to a thousand dollars of compute each (¶8); at a compute cost of ten to a thousand dollars per problem (¶94)
claims.reasoning: Exact range matches both source passages.

claims.claim_text: The one step they could not automate was choosing the problems, the judgment this post is about.
claims.evidence_quote: the one step they could not automate was choosing the problems, which is exactly the judgment this post is about (¶8)
claims.reasoning: Directly restates the source sentence.

claims.claim_text: Method: collect unpublished problems across fields, pick ten per batch, give one attempt each, grade blind with human referees.
claims.evidence_quote: They collect unpublished research problems from mathematicians across fields, pick ten for each batch ... one attempt each ... human referees grade the solutions blind (¶94)
claims.reasoning: All four method steps match the appendix description.

claims.claim_text: Early 2026: an AI system produced a machine-checked Lean proof of Erdős Problem #728.
claims.evidence_quote: In early 2026, an AI system produced a machine-checked Lean proof of Erdős Problem #728 (¶9)
claims.reasoning: Date, system type, Lean, and problem number all match.

claims.claim_text: The system combined OpenAI's GPT-5.2 Pro with Harmonic's Aristotle.
claims.evidence_quote: a system combining OpenAI's GPT-5.2 Pro with Harmonic's Aristotle (¶95)

claims.claim_text: Nat Sothanaphan translated it into a conventional argument, and the problem is now marked proved on the Erdős problems list.

claims.claim_text: May 2026: an OpenAI reasoning model disproved the planar unit distance conjecture Erdős posed in 1946.
claims.evidence_quote: in May 2026 an OpenAI model disproved the planar unit distance conjecture Erdős had posed in 1946 (¶9)
claims.reasoning: Date, entity, conjecture, and 1946 all match.

claims.claim_text: The conjecture said the maximum number of unit distances among n points in the plane grows like n^{1+o(1)}.

claims.claim_text: The model built infinite families of point sets with at least n^{1+\varepsilon} unit distances, using algebraic number theory.
claims.evidence_quote: The model constructed infinite families of point sets with at least $n^{1+\varepsilon}$ unit distances, using ideas from algebraic number theory. (¶95)
claims.reasoning: Bound and method match the appendix.

claims.claim_text: A paper with Alon, Bloom, Gowers and others digested the result for the community.
claims.evidence_quote: A paper with Alon, Bloom, Gowers and others then digested the result for the community. (¶95)
claims.reasoning: Names and action match exactly.

claims.claim_text: The split: the model produced the result, while humans checked, digested, and presented it.
claims.evidence_quote: The model produced the result, the humans checked it, digested it, and presented it. (¶10)
claims.reasoning: Directly restates the source's split.

claims.claim_text: The production of proofs has been automated, or it will be, under Tao's working assumption.
claims.evidence_quote: The production of proofs has been automated, or it will be, under Tao's working assumption. (¶10)
claims.reasoning: Verbatim restatement including the working-assumption qualifier.

claims.claim_text: Seven of ten novel problems solved to publication quality for a few hundred to a few thousand dollars of compute.
claims.evidence_quote: Seven out of ten novel research problems, solved to publication quality, for a few hundred to a few thousand dollars of compute. (¶11)
claims.reasoning: All figures match the source exactly.

claims.claim_text: What was not automated: people still chose the problems and handed them to the models one at a time.

claims.claim_text: The models still might need a lot of handholding.

claims.claim_text: Conjecture generators propose patterns, but they do not decide which ones matter.
claims.evidence_quote: they propose patterns, they do not decide which ones matter (¶11)

claims.claim_text: So either mathematics is over, or the old definition was wrong.
claims.evidence_quote: So either mathematics is over, or the old definition was wrong. (¶11)

claims.claim_text: It is not over: the author thinks it has just started, and wants to explore how the definition was wrong.

claims.claim_text: Maybe the proving was the chore and the finding was always the real thing.
